meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Forgive me, this is very important.
Lena, forgive me.
I am at fault, forgive me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was'.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
That simply cannot be!
I have a toy car.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: She is a good one you have.
Calm down, I will leave everything to a professional.
Maybe she was joking?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Но я точно знаю, что ребёнок мой.
examples.trans: But I know for sure that the child is mine.

examples.text: Дело в том, что это мой ребёнок.
examples.trans: The thing is that this is my child.
My first husband is Victor Petrovich.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Is Den married?
His wife left him.
My wife is being monitored by you.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ex-wife / former').

examples.trans: You blabber about your ex-husband.

examples.text: Моя бывшая беременна, говорит, что не от меня.
examples.trans: My ex is pregnant and says it is not mine.
It is called 'Ex-Husband.'

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Vika, wait!
We need to talk!
I know that you are pregnant!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'конец-то'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Ah, finally.
At last! I'm free!
You've finally arrived!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'better', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What happened?
That means five months ago.

examples.text: Ни в коем случае не общайтесь с ней.
examples.trans: Under no circumstances talk to her.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'здно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Better late than never.
Congratulations, daddy, a real bouncing boy.
Run, Marina, before it's too late!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'than', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me anything?

examples.text: Почему ты сам мне не рассказал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me yourself?
Why did you tell her everything?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'never', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Better late than never.
I promise, I never will again.

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to tell (a story, news)', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.text: Обо мне ведь ничего не рассказал.
examples.trans: After all, you told her nothing about me.

examples.text: Настя, ну я не могу тебе рассказать.
examples.trans: Nastya, well I cannot tell you.
Kostik told me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Calm down, I will leave everything to a professional.

examples.text: Кате всё равно правду не расскажешь.
examples.trans: You cannot tell Katya the truth anyway.
Alright, it is settled, we are going.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тебе на это ещё всю жизнь смотреть.
examples.trans: You still have to look at this your whole life.

examples.text: Витя, она мне рассказала всё ещё на выставке.
examples.trans: Vitya, she told me everything back at the exhibition.

examples.text: Мам, перестань, мы ещё толком ничего не обсудили.
examples.trans: Mom, stop it, we have not properly discussed anything yet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We need to talk!
I know that you are pregnant!
You have such a wonderful boss.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ставка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'exhibition' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Витя, она мне рассказала всё ещё на выставке.
examples.trans: Vitya, she told me everything back at the exhibition.
The exhibition is cancelled.
A representative of the exhibition from Milan called.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ещать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'promise', paired with 'пообещать'.

examples.trans: You promised, after all.
I promise, I never will again.
You do not need to promise me anything.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Я узнала о тебе много нового.
examples.trans: I learned a lot of new things about you.

examples.text: Много свободного времени, вот и занимается ерундой.
examples.trans: Lots of free time, so she busies herself with nonsense.
All the paintings were painted by me personally.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You do not need to promise me anything.

examples.text: Ну, и к чему вся эта клоунада?
examples.trans: Well, and what was all this clowning for?
Sixteen weeks.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me anything?

examples.text: Слушай, Эля, ты думаешь, я ничего не понимаю?
examples.trans: Listen, Elya, do you think I understand nothing?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: That simply cannot be!
You are simply jealous of me.

examples.text: Убедиться в том, что ребёнок твой, очень просто.
examples.trans: Making sure that the child is yours is very simple.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'паниковать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'panicked'.

examples.trans: I simply panicked.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и запаниковать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and panicked on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, afterwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Потому что он трус и лжец.
examples.trans: Because he is a coward and a liar.
And why did you not confess afterward?
First coffee, then work.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me anything?

examples.text: Почему ты сам мне не рассказал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me yourself?
And why did you not confess afterward?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'знаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'confessed / admitted', paired with 'признаваться'.

examples.text: Он хотел в чём-то мне признаться.
examples.trans: He wanted to confess something to me.
Well, did he confess?
He confessed to everything.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was afraid'.

examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.
I'm not afraid.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Poor girl, what a misfortune.

examples.text: А я вот себе туфли новые купил.
examples.trans: And I just bought myself new shoes.

examples.text: Много свободного времени, вот и занимается ерундой.
examples.trans: Lots of free time, so she busies herself with nonsense.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'говор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'conversation' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I was afraid of this very conversation.

examples.text: Денис, а ты не видишь, что мы разговариваем?
examples.trans: Denis, do you not see that we are talking?
There's an interesting conversation.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Эля, ты думаешь, я ничего не понимаю?
examples.trans: Listen, Elya, do you think I understand nothing?
Please, hear me out.

examples.text: Слушай, я забыла сумку, я быстро.
examples.trans: Listen, I forgot my bag, I will be quick.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgot', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.text: Слушай, я забыла сумку, я быстро.
examples.trans: Listen, I forgot my bag, I will be quick.
Don't forget to wash the toilet.
I forgot the keys.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'умка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'bag, handbag' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Слушай, я забыла сумку, я быстро.
examples.trans: Listen, I forgot my bag, I will be quick.
Stop, hand over the bag!
What is going on, this is my bag!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Слушай, я забыла сумку, я быстро.
examples.trans: Listen, I forgot my bag, I will be quick.
He drives fast.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('at fault, guilty').

examples.trans: In a divorce, two people are always at fault.
I am at fault, forgive me.
It's your fault!
